clue.text: Pole currently selected to play for his country provided with white top

parts.note: S is the south pole, a standard abbreviation
currently means now, at present

parts.words: selected to play for his country
parts.note: a player picked for a national side is said to be capped, after the cap awarded

explanation.surface: A Polish footballer, just picked for the national team, is handed a white cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality, but it is just S, the south pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Mountains whose summits carry snow are described this way, the white top being snow.

clue.text: It's potentially the right attitude

definitions.meaning: the right is one possible flank or edge of something, as opposed to the left
in slang, putting on airs or attitude is having swank

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain stance might be the correct one.
explanation.definitionFit: The right is one flank of a thing, and a haughty manner or swagger is an old British sense of the word.

clue.text: Departs after start before getting volunteered

indicators.note: after says the departs letter comes behind the other pieces

parts.note: the off is the start of a race, as in 'from the off'
ere is a poetic word for before
d. is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: Someone leaves after the beginning, before signing up for a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Departs' looks like a verb but is the single letter from timetables.
explanation.definitionFit: To volunteer something is to put it forward unasked, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Strengthening argument against currency valuation

parts.note: the cons are the arguments against, as in pros and cons
a cent is a unit of currency
a rating is an assessment or valuation

explanation.surface: An economist objects to valuing a currency strongly.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a solution denser or stronger by removing water is reducing it this way, so strengthening fits.

clue.text: US pupil, before very quiet, beginning to yell

parts.note: pre is the prefix meaning before
pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quiet

indicators.note: beginning to picks only the opening letter of the word yell

explanation.surface: An American schoolkid is hushed before starting to shout.
explanation.definitionFit: An American student at a private preparatory school, typically well-off and neatly dressed, is called this.

clue.text: Sailor coming in encourages one employed with soldiers?

indicators.note: coming in says the sailor goes inside the other phrase

parts.note: to egg on is to urge or encourage
PO, petty officer, is a naval rank

explanation.surface: A sailor arrives and urges on a man serving alongside troops.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain soldiers are also strips of toast dipped into a soft-boiled egg, the sense the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: You eat a boiled egg with toast fingers called soldiers and use this small utensil alongside them.

clue.text: Stagger round the bend in retreat

indicators.note: in retreat says the word for crazy goes backwards

parts.note: round the bend is slang for crazy, nuts

explanation.surface: Someone reels as they retreat around a corner in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger someone is to astonish or daze them, a synonym.

clue.text: Not any old American hero

parts.note: these, rather than those or any others, are particular ones and not just any old ones

explanation.surface: A tribute saying the hero is no ordinary American.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian slayer of the Minotaur is a hero of Greek legend.

clue.text: Concern is growing for these recklessly merry English nuns

indicators.note: recklessly says the letters are thrown about wildly into a new order

explanation.surface: Worry mounts about some carelessly jolly English nuns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concern' reads as worry, but here it means a business whose trade is growing plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Horticulturists who raise young plants for sale run a business that grows things.

clue.text: River engulfing marshland in the region of the Backs

indicators.note: engulfing says the river swallows the other pieces

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a fen is a marshland, as in the East Anglian Fens
c, circa, means about or in the region of

explanation.surface: The Cam flows through fenland past the Backs, the college lawns in Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The Backs are the riverside college grounds of Cambridge, but in sport the backs are defensive players.
explanation.definitionFit: In football or rugby the backs are the players who protect their goal, together the defensive unit.

clue.text: Break before going up in space endlessly long

parts.note: a gap is a space

indicators.note: endlessly says the last letter of the word for long is dropped

parts.note: to long for is to yearn

explanation.surface: A pause before climbing into the void, with an endless longing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going up' is British for starting at university.
explanation.definitionFit: A year out taken between school and university is a break before going up to college.

clue.text: Thoughtlessly mean corruption, leading to rage?

parts.note: par is the average or mean, as in below par
rot is decay or corruption
the rage is the fashion, as in all the rage

explanation.surface: A spiteful corruption ends up provoking fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeating words mechanically without understanding, as a talking bird does, is doing it thoughtlessly.

clue.text: Kind old man returned theatre member's programme

parts.note: an order is a kind or class, as in of a high order
pa is a familiar word for father, an old man

indicators.note: returned says the word for theatre goes backwards

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre

explanation.surface: A generous elderly man hands back an actor's playbill.
explanation.walkthrough: The member is a Member of Parliament, not a member of the theatre company.
explanation.definitionFit: The daily agenda of business in the House of Commons is the parliamentary member's programme.

clue.text: Nephew Esau accommodating Jacob? Not he!

indicators.note: accommodating says the letters sit housed within the words nephew Esau

explanation.surface: A biblical reference: Esau, Jacob's brother, putting someone up, with a denial.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacob is not the patriarch but a breed of sheep; 'Not he' asks for the female.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jacob is a piebald sheep breed, and a female sheep, not a ram, fits 'not he'.

clue.text: Bargain that's spoiled by hidden tariff

parts.note: a steal is a bargain

indicators.note: spoiled says the letters of that are wrecked into a new order

parts.note: the word that, with the 's as the link 'is'
x means by, as in a room 3 x 4

explanation.surface: A cheap deal is ruined by a concealed levy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is the multiplication sign X, as in dimensions.
explanation.definitionFit: A tax raised in a way the public barely notices is a hidden tariff, a political coinage.

clue.text: Thus far, it's the lonely heart's desire?

definitions.meaning: someone placing a lonely hearts advert wants to go out with someone, to find a romantic partner

explanation.surface: So far, what a lonely-hearts advertiser longs for.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means so far, and read literally it is the wish of a single person seeking a partner.

clue.text: Happily, the reader is embraced by a girl, and not Frank

indicators.note: is embraced by says the reader word goes inside the girl and the sly pieces

parts.note: Jo is a girl's name
not frank means sly, underhand
the reader is addressed as you

explanation.surface: A happy scene: you are hugged by a girl, and Frank is left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name, but it means candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with joy is doing it happily, a synonym.

clue.text: Sub maybe busy, with rising sea level unknown

parts.note: busy is British slang for a police officer, a cop
y is an algebraic unknown

indicators.note: rising in a down clue says the sea word reads upwards

parts.note: the tide is the level of the sea

explanation.surface: A submarine maybe, busy as the sea level climbs into the unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: A sub is a subeditor, not a submarine.
explanation.definitionFit: A subeditor on a newspaper corrects and prepares copy, the job this verb names.

clue.text: Returning American's fizzy drink, company goes for French fruit

indicators.note: Returning says all the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: soda is the American word for a fizzy drink
va is French for goes, as in il va

explanation.surface: An American returns a soft drink, and the firm goes for French fruit instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes for French' looks like a substitution but just asks for French for goes.
explanation.definitionFit: These pear-shaped green fruits with large stones are the source of guacamole.

clue.text: Something that's blown article inside damaged aircon

indicators.note: inside says the article goes within the reworked letters
damaged says the letters of aircon are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A fan inside a broken air-conditioner is blowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' makes OCRINA from AIRCON, and A goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: This small egg-shaped wind instrument is played by blowing into it.

clue.text: A source of pressure, as in exam?

indicators.note: in says the as word goes inside the exam letters

parts.note: GCE, General Certificate of Education, is a British school exam
for can mean as, in 'taken for granted'

explanation.surface: An exam as a cause of stress for students.
explanation.walkthrough: The GCE is the British school-leaving qualification, O and A levels.
explanation.definitionFit: The force of acceleration felt by pilots presses on the body, so it is a source of pressure.

clue.text: Was onto liquor, then did milk

parts.note: rum is a liquor
to milk someone is to bleed them dry of money

explanation.surface: A farmhand who had been on the rum and then did the milking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was onto' means had found someone out, not was drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: To be onto someone is to have seen through them, and the answer means found out.

clue.text: One starting top

definitions.meaning: someone who starts or leaps up in alarm, one who jumps
a top is a garment for the upper body, such as a pullover

explanation.definitionFit: A pullover is a knitted top in British English, and a person who leaps is also this.

clue.text: Leaves career unfulfilled

indicators.note: unfulfilled says the word for career lacks its final letter

parts.note: to career is to tear along at speed

explanation.surface: Someone quits a job that never satisfied them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as a verb but is the noun: dried leaves for brewing.
explanation.definitionFit: The dried leaves of the plant are what is brewed, often sold loose as leaves.

clue.text: Fake IOU's my undoing, in my opinion

indicators.note: undoing says these letters are taken apart and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A forged promissory note brought about my downfall.
explanation.definitionFit: This conversational phrase introduces a personal view, the same as saying in my opinion.

clue.text: He has no right to get upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue says the pieces are turned upside down

parts.note: nay is an old word for no

explanation.surface: A man with no right to be angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is the definition: any man's name, here a common boy's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's given name defines as 'he', a male person, a crossword convention for names.

clue.text: Caught on tape removing copy, reprimanded

indicators.note: removing says the copy word is taken out of the word tape

parts.note: to ape is to copy
to wig is to scold, reprimand

explanation.surface: Someone captured on video, with the copy deleted, was told off.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch on is to understand, and this slang verb means grasped or realised.

clue.text: Foot extended about an inch for pattern

indicators.note: extended about says the foot word is stretched around the island word

parts.note: to foot a bill is to pay it
an inch is a Scottish word for a small island

explanation.surface: A measuring note: a foot lengthened by around an inch for a design.
explanation.walkthrough: Foot and inch look like units, but foot is a verb and an inch is a Scottish isle.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a swirling teardrop textile design named after a Scottish town.

clue.text: When to follow Mass times, reflecting?

definitions.text: When to follow Mass times, reflecting?

indicators.note: to follow says the when word comes after the others
reflecting says the mass and times pieces are seen as in a mirror, backwards

parts.note: m is the abbreviation for mass in physics
x is the multiplication sign, times
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A question about when to go to Mass, and pondering the times.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: Christmas is literally Christ's Mass, a season for reflection.
explanation.definitionFit: The festival's name comes from Christ's Mass, so it is the time for following Mass.

clue.text: Ancient flyer, a sort of ad, torn open

indicators.note: a sort of says the letters are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: An old leaflet, a kind of advert, ripped open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flyer' looks like a leaflet, matching ad, but it is a winged reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: This toothless winged reptile of the Cretaceous flew over prehistoric seas.
